directive.quote: Build a new Workshop tool start-a-place: makes and starts one Trillion place on this computer.

job: Make this machine into a Trillion computer and start it: its key, its config and the running engine

distinct_from.why: This tool itself: its README, rows and tests name the engine commands it runs.
This tool's own capability row: its evidence names the `trillion-local serve` command this tool runs. It is the registry entry for this tool, not another owner of the job.
The generated tool catalog (publish-tool-catalog.mjs): it carries this tool's own row, whose description names `trillion-local serve`. A generated listing of this tool, not another owner of the job.

The engine's command line: it parses `trillion-local serve PLACE_CONFIG` and runs one computer from a config that already exists. It makes no key and writes no config; this tool makes both and then calls it.
The engine's computer entry: it reads and checks a computer config and serves it. It is what this tool's config is written for, and it creates nothing (no key, no folder, no config).

Adds a computer to an account (`computer id`, `send-root`, `freeze`, `join`) at a computer whose config and key already exist; this tool calls its `computer id` once and makes the config and key it reads.
A sign-up at a running computer; it reads the config's computer key file, it does not make a computer.
Makes an account at a computer (`account create PLACE_CONFIG`), not the computer.
Reads a computer key file (base64 on one line) into the vault root; it never makes one.
The computer key's size and file limit, read by root.rs; this tool's settings name the same size.
Recovery of an account's lease under a process; it names `trillion-local serve` only as the process that holds the lease.
Which process owns a record store; it names `trillion-local serve` only as one such process.
The engine's own test computer: a config and key written inside a Rust test for one process. Its values are this tool's defaults; it is not a tool a person runs.
Status notes of the placement work that describe `trillion-local serve` and `computer id`; words, not a way to make a computer.
A status note that says a computer runs with no hosting app; words, not a way to make one.

phrasings: Make a Trillion computer on this computer and start it: its key, its config and the running computer
start trillion-local serve with a computer config
write a computer config and a computer key file
start a computer and print its computer id with trillion-local computer id
